_note: Copy to .claude/kit.json in your project. Every key is optional; delete what you don't need. Skills fall back to built-in defaults when a key or the whole file is absent.
_note_mode: outside = kit files are symlinks to your kit checkout and are meant to stay out of git (install.sh prints the .gitignore lines and never writes them). inside = kit files are real files, tracked in git, travel with the repo. Choose inside if a machine without your kit checkout needs this repo to work.
_note_kitPath: Optional override for where the kit lives. Resolution order: $TB_CLAUDE_KIT, then this key, then ~/.claude-kit, then the folder install.sh is in. Leave unset unless this project needs a different checkout than the rest.
_note_fork: Paths this project owns outright. They EXIST here, but the kit never touches them: real files instead of symlinks in outside mode, skipped by drift detection in inside mode. Prefer the other lanes below — fork is a last resort for when kit behavior itself must change.
_note_exclude: Paths that should NOT exist in this project at all — never installed, in either mode. Use to install a subset of the kit, e.g. a repo for a non-technical user that should not carry developer skills. Different from fork: fork means 'the project owns this', exclude means 'this does not belong here'. Excluding does not delete what is already on disk; install.sh reports leftovers so you can remove them deliberately.
_note_memory: Where Claude Code keeps this project's auto-memory. By default the kit keeps it in the repo, at .claude/memory, committed with it, rather than in the machine's config folder where it is lost with the machine. install.sh (both modes) and the session-start hook (outside mode, on the next session) set autoMemoryDirectory in .claude/settings.local.json, which is per machine and gitignored (never the checked-in settings.json, where Claude Code ignores it). Memories already in the config folder are copied across without overwriting, and the old folder is kept beside a link to the new one. inRepo: false turns this off. It stops enforcing and never undoes a setup; install.sh says what to remove by hand. null (the default) means on, except that a repo whose origin is a PUBLIC GitHub repo is left alone, because memories hold personal notes. true means on even then.
_note_kill: Ports and patterns for /kill. portRanges are inclusive pairs. patterns are extra pgrep -f arguments. scopeToProjectPath additionally kills node/tsx processes whose command line contains this project's path.
_note_clearCache: For /clear-cache. projectRoots: where your projects live; the deep tier looks there for stale node_modules. staleDays: a project with no file changed in this many days counts as stale (deep tier only).
_note_prune: For /prune. staleDays: a worktree with no commit and no file change for this many days is offered for removal. keep: branch-name globs /prune never recommends removing.
_note_commit: Pins the commit author for /commit. Sets --author only, so the committer still comes from git config and the two identities will differ. Most projects should omit this.
_note_subtrees: Folders that are also pushed to a repo of their own. `/commit sub <name>` and `/push sub <name>` push that entry's prefix to its remote and branch after committing. Each entry: prefix (the folder), remote (a git remote name), branch (default main). Example: { "app": { "prefix": "app", "remote": "app", "branch": "main" } }.
_note_secrets: Which 1Password vault holds this project's secrets, for ~/.claude-kit/scripts/oprun. One read-only service account per vault (created by op-sa-bootstrap <vault>), token in the macOS Keychain as op-sa-<vault>, never exported globally. account is only used by op-sa-bootstrap to pick the 1Password account the vault lives in.
_note_plan: Directories /plan may write to. May contain * wildcards. Subdirectories of a root are found automatically and do not need listing. Numbering is per-directory; plan_id becomes <scope>-NNN for scoped plans.

plan._note_issues: Tracker settings for /plan's epic and issue modes (PR-mode plans). publish: ahead = `/plan NNN epic` puts every slice on the tracker as a sub-issue before building starts; on-start (default) = the epic alone, and each slice's issue is created by `/plan NNN issue <slice>` when it starts. repo: the tracker repo when it is not this one. assignee and labels go on every issue created; neverLabels are labels the team's automation acts on (an agent queue, an auto-close rule) and are never applied. check: a command that lints a body file before posting, with {file} and {kind} (epic, issue, pr, comment) filled in. sweep: the prior-art sweep agent or script. No issue is created and nobody is mentioned without the owner's go; refreshing the body of an existing issue does not wait.

_note_research: Same as plan.roots, for /research output folders.
_note_web: Where /web looks for the built static site, and the canonical origin it checks URLs against. roots is a candidate list; the first directory that exists and contains HTML wins. Absent, /web tries web, public, dist, site, build, _site, out, sitemd/site, then the project root. baseUrl is required for canonical/sitemap URL checks and for /web live. ignore records divergences you have decided are correct so re-runs stop re-reporting them — each rule needs check, plus optional file and match (substring of the message) to narrow it, and a note explaining the call. Suppressed findings are still counted and listed under --show-suppressed, never silently dropped.
_note_wiki: Configuration for /wiki. root is the wiki directory (default: wiki/). styleScaffold is a path to a STYLE.md template that /wiki init copies when creating a new wiki — lets an organization maintain a standard starting point while allowing per-project evolution. pagesProject is the Cloudflare Pages project /wiki deploy publishes to (default: <repo-name>-wiki). title is the wiki's name, shown at the top of the sidebar and the end of every tab title (default: the index's first heading). renderer is a command /wiki deploy uses to render the parsed wiki bundle instead of the kit's plain renderer; it runs from the project root with the bundle directory and the output directory appended (see the README's "wiki.json format"). All keys are optional.
_note_swarm: Configuration for /swarm autonomous plan execution. maxAgents caps how many unit agents run concurrently during a swarm run (setup can override per-run with user approval). checks is the project's verification command list — reviewer agents run these verbatim on every unit; when absent, swarm setup determines the commands itself and records them in SWARM.md. Agents always verify UI by code first and in a headless browser of their own second; none of them verifies in a headed browser. The rest matter for PR-mode plans in a team repo. ship: ready = the owner has pre-approved ready PRs; draft = every PR opens as a draft; ask (default) = the ship command asks, so setup settles it once. look: none (default) = user-facing slices ship without waiting for the owner; batch = they park for one batch look; per-slice = each parks and notifies on its own. review: the team's own review tool, run against a pushed PR (<pr> is filled in); it replaces the swarm's reviewer agent. watch: the project's CI watcher, which reruns a red caused by CI's own infrastructure before any fix agent is sent. resources: path globs mapped to tags for shared local state (a fixed-port dev server, the one local database, the package install); two units holding the same tag never run at once.

swarm._note_worktree: Only when the code lives in a checkout OUTSIDE the session's repo (a sibling clone, a symlink, a submodule). create and remove are the commands that make and delete a unit's worktree there, with <slug> and <branch> filled in; put it at .claude/worktrees/<slug> in that repo and include the repo's own bootstrap in create. pool is for a big repository: units lease a slot that was bootstrapped once instead of creating a worktree each. Its acquire, release and list commands get <lane>, <branch>, <base> and <slot> filled in, and size is the number of slots (the concurrency cap plus two is a good start). Example: { "create": "git -C ../app worktree add .claude/worktrees/<slug> -b <branch> origin/main", "remove": "git -C ../app worktree remove .claude/worktrees/<slug>", "pool": { "acquire": "scripts/slot.sh acquire <lane> <branch> <base>", "release": "scripts/slot.sh release <slot>", "list": "scripts/slot.sh list", "size": 8 } }.
swarm._note_reviewStack: How /swarm review serves the owner's look. Every key is optional; without them the review asks once how to start an app. <app> and <checkout> are filled in. shared: a command that exits 0 when the stack every app sits behind (a proxy, an auth service) is up. sharedStart: how to start it when it is down. serve: the long-running command that serves one app from one checkout. port: a command printing the port that app listens on. tag: the resource tag a served app holds, matching swarm.resources (e.g. port:<app>). holdAlso: tags the whole review holds, such as the local database its fixtures live in. restore: path globs the dev server rewrites in a checkout, restored when a server stops. logs: the directory server logs go to.

_note_sqlite_tracking: SQLite databases that get NDJSON snapshot files on /commit, using the AirSQLite sidecar layout: {dbname}.airsqlite/{table}.snapshot.ndjson. Each entry is { "db": "path/to/file.db", "tables": [...], "exclude": [...] }: db is the .db file, tables is which tables to track (default: all non-internal tables), and exclude is table-name globs to leave out, such as logs_fts*. One JSON line per row (including _rowid), sorted by rowid. Regenerated before staging, not as a git hook.
_note_rules: Short project-specific instructions, keyed by skill name. Each skill reads its own entry and applies it. Skills that read one: 1password, brain, brainstorm, bridge, claude-switcher, clear-cache, commit, cto, kill, look, parse, pbar, plan, prune, push, research, swarm, vibe-audit, video-editor, web, wiki. rules.plan is where a team repo's ship command and policy, branch conventions, priority tiers and CI path map go; rules.look names the base URL and how a fresh headless profile signs in. Keep these to a sentence or two — a rule that needs more room belongs in a project-owned skill with its own name, or upstream in the kit.

rules.push: Example: if the post-commit hook reports undeployed worker changes, ask before pushing — never auto-deploy.
